title: DockerSSD: Containerized In-Storage Processing and Hardware Acceleration for Computational SSDs
problem: In-storage processing systems are vendor-specific, require source-level application modification, and face practical challenges including limited processing capabilities and security vulnerabilities at the storage level.
motivation: In-storage processing reduces energy consumption by enabling data examination near storage, avoiding costly data movement to host processors for massive datasets.
method: DockerSSD implements OS-level virtualization in SSDs through a novel communication protocol and virtual firmware that enables unmodified Docker images to execute as containers in storage. Container lifecycle management operates transparently without changing existing storage interfaces, while dedicated hardware acceleration optimizes container-related network and I/O data paths.
key_novelty: Enabling Docker containers as first-class execution environments in commodity SSDs, eliminating vendor-specific implementations and enabling reuse of existing containerized applications.
contributions: Flexible in-storage processing model supporting diverse applications without source-level modification
OS-level containerization infrastructure for commodity SSDs with transparent Docker image support
Novel communication protocol and virtual firmware for container management without storage interface modification
Hardware acceleration for container I/O and network data paths
primary_theme: Containerized in-storage processing with hardware acceleration
